title: 21. Numeracy & Number Systems: Integer Addition Using Number Lines
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the result of adding a positive integer by moving right on a number line.
questions.question: On a number line, start at \(-3\) and move \(5\) units to the right. Where do you land?
questions.explanation: On a number line, adding a positive integer means moving to the right. Start at \(-3\) and move \(5\) units right: \(-3 + 5 = 2\). Therefore, you land on \(2\).
questions.hint: Moving right on a number line represents adding a positive integer.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the result of adding a negative integer by moving left on a number line.
questions.question: On a number line, start at \(4\) and move \(7\) units to the left. Where do you land?
questions.explanation: On a number line, adding a negative integer means moving to the left. Start at \(4\) and move \(7\) units left: \(4 + (-7) = -3\). Therefore, you land on \(-3\).
questions.hint: Moving left on a number line represents adding a negative integer.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a sum of a negative integer and a positive integer using a number line.
questions.question: What is \(-6 + 4\) using a number line?
questions.explanation: Start at \(-6\) on the number line. Since \(4\) is positive, move \(4\) units to the right: \(-6 + 4 = -2\). Therefore, the sum is \(-2\).
questions.hint: Start at the first integer, then move right for the positive addend.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a sum of a positive integer and a negative integer using a number line.
questions.question: What is \(3 + (-8)\) using a number line?
questions.explanation: Start at \(3\) on the number line. Since \(-8\) is negative, move \(8\) units to the left: \(3 + (-8) = -5\). Therefore, the sum is \(-5\).
questions.hint: Start at the first integer, then move left for the negative addend.

questions.learningObjective: Identify an addition expression that represents moving left on a number line.
questions.question: Which expression represents starting at \(-2\) and moving \(6\) units to the left on a number line?
questions.explanation: Moving to the left on a number line means adding a negative integer. Starting at \(-2\) and moving \(6\) units left is represented by \(-2 + (-6)\). Therefore, the correct expression is \(-2 + (-6)\).
questions.hint: Moving left makes the value smaller. Which kind of number, when added, makes a value smaller?

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate the sum of two negative integers using a number line.
questions.question: What is \(-5 + (-3)\) using a number line?
questions.explanation: Start at \(-5\) on the number line. Since \(-3\) is negative, move \(3\) units to the left: \(-5 + (-3) = -8\). Therefore, the sum is \(-8\).
questions.hint: Adding a negative integer moves the position farther left.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the addition expression that describes a move from one integer to another.
questions.question: On a number line, a move starts at \(1\) and ends at \(-4\). Which addition expression describes this move?
questions.explanation: The move starts at \(1\) and ends at \(-4\), so the position decreases by \(5\). Moving \(5\) units left represents adding \(-5\). Therefore, the expression is \(1 + (-5)\).
questions.hint: Compare the starting and ending positions to decide whether the move is left or right.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a sum of a negative integer and a larger positive integer using a number line.
questions.question: What is \(-7 + 10\) using a number line?
questions.explanation: Start at \(-7\) on the number line. Since \(10\) is positive, move \(10\) units to the right: \(-7 + 10 = 3\). Therefore, the sum is \(3\).
questions.hint: Start at the first integer. In which direction do you move when the number being added is positive?

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a multi-step integer addition using a number line.
questions.question: On a number line, start at \(-4\), add \(9\), and then add \(-6\). Where do you end?
questions.explanation: Start at \(-4\). Add \(9\) by moving \(9\) units right: \(-4 + 9 = 5\). Then add \(-6\) by moving \(6\) units left: \(5 + (-6) = -1\). Therefore, you end at \(-1\).
questions.hint: Perform the moves one at a time in the order given.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret the meaning of adding a positive integer on a number line.
questions.question: Which description matches \(-8 + 3\) on a number line?

options.label: A
options.text: Start at \(-8\) and move \(3\) units to the left.

options.label: B
options.text: Start at \(-8\) and move \(3\) units to the right.

questions.explanation: The expression \(-8 + 3\) means starting at \(-8\) and adding positive \(3\). On a number line, adding a positive integer means moving to the right. Therefore, the correct description is to start at \(-8\) and move \(3\) units to the right.
questions.hint: The sign of the added integer tells the direction of the move.
